page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs with a combined total of 320 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not included on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in passmark CPU score (85,426.66) and passmark CPU extended instructions (117,918.35). Memory bandwidth read-only small block performance reached a top-tier 7,649.82 GB/sec, while large block read and write bandwidths registered at 316.04 GB/sec and 135.84 GB/sec respectively. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the system demonstrated top-tier capabilities, processing 10,308.98 tokens/sec for prompts and generating 377.14 tokens/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier at 2,196.39.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of system memory combined with 320 GB of H100 VRAM provides a resource-dense platform for large-scale parallel processing without the overhead of dedicated CPU cores. This server is designed for workloads such as large language model inference, deep learning training, parallel scientific simulations, and memory-intensive GPU-accelerated database operations.
